ai.description: This small snake reaches 30 cm. It has a glossy, iridescent black dorsum and a bright red venter. A distinctive feature is its short, blunt tail ending in a small, keratinized terminal scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Teretrurus rhodogaster* is uniquely identified by its bright red or orange underside, which contrasts sharply with its dark, iridescent brown or blackish dorsal scales.
ai.habitat: The Palni Mountain Burrowing Snake inhabits high-altitude shola forests and grassy slopes in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 2,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Palni Mountain burrowing snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time underground to navigate its humid, high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Palni Mountain Burrowing Snake is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically around June.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Palni Mountain burrowing snake is endemic to the high-elevation grasslands and shola forests of the Palni Hills in Tamil Nadu, India.
